data.narrative:
Nara Space Technology is a publicly listed South Korean space and aerospace company founded by Park Jae-pil. The valuation exercise draws from a comparable universe of 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private competitors including Planet Labs, Astroscale, and SpaceX, representing 13 total data points in the Space & Aerospace sector.

Neither standard triangulation method is applicable to this target. The Peer-Median approach is inapplicable because the narrow peer set—filtered by stage and valuation tier—yields fewer than three comparable companies. The Public-Comp Anchoring method, while supported by a sector P/S median of 23.9x across the 6 public comparables, cannot be executed because Nara's revenue is not on file. Private companies in this sector typically do not disclose revenue, blocking this calculation.

Without executable valuation methods, no specific valuation range can be derived from the available data. The primary uncertainty is the absence of Nara's revenue figure, which is essential for any market-multiple approach. A secondary constraint is the thinly distributed peer set at the same stage and valuation tier. To proceed with valuation, either Nara's revenue disclosure or a willingness to anchor to broader sector multiples (accepting greater estimation error) would be required.
